text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
-- The U.S: supports only Poalnd, the Czech Republic and Hungary in the first round of expansion of NATO, a White House spokesman said.
-- Government spokesman Elemer Kiss said that the gopvernment anticipates a 13.5 percent rate of inflation and 3.5 percent economic growth next year.
-- Deputy Speaker of Parliament Tibor Fuzessy announced Thursday that the government has requested a special session of Parliament to ve convened from june 15 to July 31.

-- Free Democrat MPO Andrea Szolnoki said that if no dramatic improvement comes soon in the running of the social security authorities, her parliamentary group will call for the dissolution of the authorities.
-- Opposition Young Democrat leader Viktor Orban called on President Arpad Goncz to convene parliamentary elections at the earliest possible date next year.
-- The industry ministry said exports and imports went up by 10.3 and 12 percent respectively in January-April from the same period of 1996.
-- Thed Hungarian economy may expand by 3.5 percent next year, overtaking the Czech Republic, according to the latest study by the Organisation for economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
-- It would be disadvantageous to Hungary if the Euiropean Union were would begin simultaneous accession negotiations with every associate country, Agrficultural Minister Frigyes Nagy said.

-- American company Danco Laboratories Ltd sued Hungarian drug maker Richter for cancelling an agreement on production of the much debated dryug RY 486, which causes a spontaneous abortion in the early stages of pregnancy.
-- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will meet representatives of the four Hungarian historical churches prior to signing an agreement with the Vatican next Friday.
